claims.text: R0637's research profile covers electromagnetic compatibility, printed circuit board radiation, signal integrity, pre-compliance EMI, FDTD modelling, near-field scanning and power delivery network topics, and her group uses a vector network analyser, near-field scanning bench and faculty-licensed FDTD/MoM solvers.
limitations: Profile-level description; not evidence that these tools or capacities are currently available for an external project.

claims.text: She co-authored a study of a rule-based layout scoring tool that ingests Gerber files and a netlist, extracts emission-risk geometry features, and outputs a score plus a flagged violation list; on 23 boards of known emission performance it flagged 19 of 23 CISPR 22 Class B failures (83% sensitivity) with a 22% false-positive rate, and the authors describe it as an early design gate rather than a replacement for simulation or pre-compliance measurement.
limitations: Validation set is 23 boards of unspecified origin and complexity; sensitivity/false-positive figures are from that set only and not transferable to Nexara's boards without re-validation.

claims.text: A co-authored integrated pre-compliance workflow sequentially combines automated layout rule checking, near-field scanning at 3 mm standoff, and FDTD simulation of identified hotspots; across four prototype boards from two regional companies it identified the dominant emission source in every case, corrective measures reduced peak radiated emission at the pre-compliance receiver by 5.2–11.7 dB, and time-to-compliance averaged 2.1 fewer test-and-rework cycles versus a historical baseline, with workflow documentation and rule-checker code openly deposited.
limitations: Four-board sample with partner-provided prototypes; the 2.1-cycle comparison is against an unspecified historical baseline, not a controlled trial.

claims.text: She led a project that developed and validated a structured pre-compliance methodology for predicting radiated and conducted emissions from mixed-signal PCBs before formal certification, covering automated layout rule checking, near-field scan processing and far-field transformation, and parametric FDTD simulation libraries, validated on faculty test vehicles and prototypes from two Vojvodina electronics manufacturers, producing an open-source rule checker.
limitations: Project summary text; individual deliverables and their availability for re-use are not documented here.

claims.text: Related co-authored measurements show that distributed 100 nF decoupling at 5 mm spacing reduced peak PDN impedance from 840 mΩ to 210 mΩ at 480 MHz with a corresponding 4.8 dB broadband noise-floor reduction between 400 and 600 MHz, and that 3 mm-standoff near-field scans reached 85% rank-order agreement with OATS results at each board's maximum-emission frequency (absolute agreement within ±4.5 dB in 74% of cases, degrading to ±9 dB above 700 MHz).
limitations: Test-vehicle and seven-board consumer-electronics samples; results are not proven for Nexara's board types, stack-ups or 150–450 MHz failure bands specifically.

claims.text: Her documented open_to list includes contract research on PCB EMC characterisation and pre-compliance testing, consulting on EMC design review and CISPR compliance strategies, joint projects combining simulation with industrial prototype testing, and equipment access to the near-field scan bench and vector network analyser; her industry experience includes two contract research engagements with regional electronics manufacturers and informal EMC consultations in the NTP Novi Sad cluster.
limitations: Stated interests rather than confirmed commitments for this specific engagement.

claims.text: The Gerber-plus-netlist rule checker and the near-field/FDTD workflow jointly address the gap Nexara describes (pre-compliance scans miss systematic layout review), since both operate on design data Nexara already holds and target engineers running checks themselves before sign-off rather than one-off consultancy reviews; the documented 150 MHz–1 GHz operating ranges of the scan and rule-checking work overlap Nexara's 150–450 MHz band.
limitations: No evidence addresses Nexara's specific boards, their HyperLynx-only toolchain, or the €9,000/retest economics; overlap is thematic, not validated on Nexara data.

claims.text: Bounded pilot: run the open rule scorer over Nexara's five archived boards (Gerber + BOM + pre-compliance scan data under NDA) to test whether its flagged violations cluster on the three failed boards and at 150–450 MHz, then apply the near-field scan + FDTD spot analysis to the top flagged hotspot on two boards to check whether it predicts the lab-observed emission; milestones are (M1) data intake and baseline scoring of all five boards, (M2) hotspot diagnosis on two boards, (M3) a drafted layout checklist subset and a written simulation workflow for Nexara's engineers to apply via HyperLynx plus the rule tool.
limitations: Pilot scope, milestones and effort are proposed, not agreed; a five-board retrospective is too small to establish general prediction accuracy.

claims.text: Validation design: baseline is Nexara's existing practice (pre-compliance scan plus impedance-check-only simulation) and the boards' known pass/fail outcomes; measurements are rule-score/violation counts per board versus failure status, hotspot localization agreement (dominant source correctly identified), and predicted versus observed emission frequency and amplitude at the lab, with go/no-go set as: the scorer must flag all three known failing boards (or, if it misses one, the miss must be explained by a rule gap that is then closed); hotspot analysis must identify the dominant source on at least one of two boards; and every proposed checklist item must be actionable by Nexara's own layout engineers without the research team present.
limitations: Thresholds are proposed acceptance criteria to be negotiated; the 83%/22% published figures do not guarantee these thresholds on Nexara boards.

claims.text: Constraints and participation conditions: Nexara must provide the Gerber, BOM, stack-up, netlist and pre-compliance scan data plus failure descriptions under NDA, and nominate one senior hardware engineer to co-develop and apply the checklist; the near-field bench is available only on a cost-recovery basis and subject to faculty teaching commitments, faculty solvers are licensed through the university, and no current scheduling capacity is confirmed, so a time plan and confidentiality terms must be agreed before work starts.
limitations: Bench availability, cost-recovery rates, licensing terms for using faculty solvers on company data, and any timeline are unconfirmed and must be settled with the company and the faculty.

claims.text: Unresolved requirements not covered by this evidence: translating the open rule checker into Nexara's HyperLynx-centric flow (script/toolchain integration, IT approval of Python tooling), handling any board features outside the tool's 17 documented rules, and demonstrating that a checklist trained on five local boards generalizes to future client designs; also whether conducted-emission or enclosure-resonance effects dominate above 700 MHz, where the near-field method degrades.
limitations: These are open gaps in the evidence, not claims that they cannot be solved; resolving them needs Nexara-specific data and possibly additional work beyond the pilot.

summary.text: R0637 is a strong technical match: her co-authored work combines a Gerber/netlist-based automated emission-risk rule checker with an integrated layout-check, near-field scanning and FDTD workflow validated on real prototype boards, which maps directly onto Nexara's need for a systematic, engineer-runnable pre-layout emissions review and their 150–450 MHz failure band.

This is a partial, pilot-level match: no evidence covers Nexara's own boards, their HyperLynx-only toolchain, or the cost/delay economics, and bench and faculty-solver availability must be confirmed before commitments.

technicalRationale.text: The rule checker ingests Gerber and netlist data and flags geometric emission risks with reported 83% sensitivity and 22% false positives on 23 known boards, giving a fast early design gate; the workflow paper adds near-field scanning and FDTD hotspot quantification, which produced dominant-source identification on all four partner boards and 5.2–11.7 dB measured reductions.
The underlying project produced an open-source rule checker and documented workflow, supporting the goal of a method Nexara's engineers run themselves rather than per-board consultancy.
Her PDN and near-field-to-far-field work provides diagnostic background relevant to the 150–450 MHz range, though it was validated on different board populations and degrades above 700 MHz.

cooperationScope.text: Proposed pilot contributions: (M1) data intake under NDA and baseline rule scoring of all five Nexara boards; (M2) near-field scan plus FDTD spot analysis of the top flagged hotspot on two boards; (M3) a draft layout checklist subset and a written simulation workflow Nexara's layout engineers can run with HyperLynx and the open rule tool. Work is delivered to Nexara's team, not as one-off board reviews.

validation.text: Baseline: Nexara's current pre-compliance-plus-impedance-check practice and the five boards' known pass/fail outcomes. Measure rule scores and violation lists versus failure status, dominant-source identification on the two analysed boards, and predicted vs observed frequency/amplitude at the lab. Go/no-go: all three failing boards flagged (or each miss explained and the rule gap closed), dominant source correctly identified on at least one of two boards, and each checklist item executable by Nexara engineers unaided.

constraints.text: Required inputs: Gerber, BOM, stack-up, netlist, pre-compliance scan data and failure descriptions for the five boards under NDA, plus one nominated senior hardware engineer. Participation conditions: near-field bench use on a cost-recovery basis and only when teaching commitments permit; use of faculty-licensed FDTD/MoM solvers on company data requires licensing confirmation; dates and terms are unconfirmed.

unknowns.text: Open questions: how the open rule checker integrates with Nexara's HyperLynx flow and IT policy; whether the 17 documented rules cover Nexara's board features; whether a five-board retrospective supports generalizable prediction; whether enclosure or conducted paths dominate in specific 150–450 MHz failures; and confirmed bench access, solver licensing, cost and timeline.
